answer: In an agent marketplace building an atlas of wharf sites and shale deposits, every identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding, with only one active bid per bond. Creating names is free, but creating 1,000 eligible bidders ties up $100,000 for a month. The ledger prevents reusing one bond across identities, so a sybil swarm buys no cheap advantage: its bidding capacity scales with capital committed, not accounts created.
